2007 French Open Women’s Doubles Champions

Alicia Molik and Mara Santangelo clinched the women’s doubles title at Roland Garros in 2007. In this iconic photograph, the two athletes stand side by side on the clay court, beaming as they hold the large silver trophy aloft. The empty stands behind them underscore the celebratory moment immediately following their victory.

This image, sourced from Getty Images and featured on the official WTA website, captures the culmination of their partnership and success at one of tennis’s four Grand Slam tournaments. The players’ matching smiles and the gleaming cup symbolize their achievement on the Parisian stage.

sourceExcerpt:
Justine Henin’s Roland Garros Triumph

Justine Henin, wearing a pink shirt and white cap, proudly holds the silver Coupe Suzanne Lenglen after winning the women’s singles title at the French Open. The trophy’s engraved plate lists champions from 1996 through 2006, including Henin’s own victories in 2003, 2005, and 2006. Her bright smile and the gleaming surface of the cup highlight the significance of this Grand Slam achievement.

This image appears in the context of a Sportskeeda feature on players who have won three Grand Slam tournaments but never captured Wimbledon. Henin’s multiple French Open titles underscore her clay-court prowess, even as the article notes her elusive quest for grass-court glory at SW19.
